title: MVTec LOCO AD overview
text: MVTec LOCO AD is a benchmark for unsupervised anomaly detection and localization in industrial inspection. It contains 3644 images from five industrial categories and includes both structural and logical anomalies. Pixel-precise ground-truth data is provided for anomalous regions.
source: MVTec LOCO AD official dataset page

title: Structural anomalies
text: Structural anomalies are visible defects affecting the physical appearance of manufactured products. Examples include scratches, dents, and contaminations. These anomalies can often be associated with localized changes in the visual appearance of a product.
source: MVTec LOCO AD official dataset page

title: Logical anomalies
text: Logical anomalies violate an underlying constraint of a product configuration. Examples include a permissible object being present in an invalid location or a required object being absent. Logical anomalies therefore depend on relationships, presence, quantity, or configuration rather than only local surface appearance.
source: MVTec LOCO AD official dataset page

title: Logical anomaly: missing required object
text: A logical anomaly can occur when an object that is required by the intended product configuration is not present. The visual appearance of the remaining components may still look normal, so detecting the anomaly requires reasoning about the expected configuration.
source: MVTec LOCO AD official dataset page

title: Logical anomaly: invalid object location
text: A logical anomaly can occur when an otherwise permissible object appears in an invalid location. The object itself may look visually normal, but its position violates an underlying product constraint.
source: MVTec LOCO AD official dataset page

title: Logical constraints require global context
text: Logical anomaly detection can require reasoning about relationships among multiple components rather than comparing only isolated local appearance. This makes global configuration and contextual information important for identifying some industrial anomalies.
source: MVTec LOCO AD official dataset page

title: Structural anomaly localization
text: Structural anomalies such as scratches, dents, or contamination can manifest as localized visual differences. Patch-level visual representations can therefore provide useful evidence for locating regions that differ from normal product appearance.
source: Derived from MVTec LOCO AD anomaly definition

title: Structural versus logical anomaly reasoning
text: Structural anomalies primarily concern abnormal physical appearance, while logical anomalies concern violations of an expected configuration or constraint. A system designed for both types should therefore consider both local visual evidence and higher-level contextual or relational information.
source: MVTec LOCO AD official dataset page

title: Breakfast box category
text: Breakfast box is one of the five industrial inspection categories in the MVTec LOCO AD benchmark. The category contains both structural and logical anomalies and is evaluated using normal images together with anomalous test images.
source: MVTec LOCO AD official dataset page
